newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 18.
newsitem.headline: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
QUEEN SHOULD SKIP AMRITSAR: PRIME MINISTER

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said the British Queen should not visit Amritsar, the scene of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919. Being a goodwill vist, India would not like to add anything historically that would cause bitterness, Gujral said. As part of her visit in October this year to mark the 50th anniversary of India's Independence, the Queen was due to visit Amritsar.
The Economic Times
TATA INDUSTRIES TIGHTENS HOLD ON KEY TECH FIRMS

Tata Industries has tightened its hold over key technology companies of the Tata group in 1996/97. These include Tata Telecom, Tata Honeywell and Tata Communications. Tata Industries, holding company for most unquoted technoloogy companies in the Tata group, has also invested in two new companies: Abacus Distribution Systems (India) and Aviation Software Development Consultancy India.
PROMOTERS ASKED TO PUT BRAKES ON PROPOSED LOCAL AREA BANKS

The Reserve Bank of India has asked the promoters of the three private sector local area banks (LAB) to put their plans on hold. These promoters already have the apex bank's in-principle approvals. But the bank has asked the promoters to await a report by the department of supervision (DOS) on their financial details before they can commence operations.
Financial Express
W.M. LEWIS NAMED CONSULTANTS FOR INDO-BANGLA POWER PROJECT

Asian development bank has appointed W.M. Lewis and Associates as technical assistance consultants for the Indo-Bangladesh power exchange project. The major role of the consultants will be to examine the commercial aspects of the power exchange project between the two countries. The consultant will moderate the discussions between the executing agencies from the two countries. It will also assist them in arriving at a fair and equitable settlement based on international commercial practices for sale and purchase of power between the two utilities.
HONDA-SIEL SEEKS NOD TO IMPORT COMPONENTS DIRECTLY

Honda-Siel, the Indian subsidiary of auto major Honda Motor of Japan, has sought permission to import components directly for its car, scheduled for a launch next year. If this proposal is cleared by the government, decks may also be cleared for companies like Daewoo Motors and PAL-Peugeot. Moreover, Honda-SIEL India has not signed a memorandum of understanding with the director general of foreign trade in the absence of a clear policy.
Business Standard
RELIANCE THE BENCHMARK FOR DOLLAR DEBT

In the absence of any sovereign flotations, the yield curves on the external debt offerings of Reliance Industries are serving as the de facto benchmark for all Indian borrowings. Fund managers have made out a strong case for a sovereign borrowing by the government to create a benchmark. They believe that this may prove critical at a time when there has been a sharp rise in the demand for debt paper from the emerging markets.
AUDIT PANELS TO BE MANDATORY FOR LARGE FIRMS

The Companies Bill 1997, which was tabled in Parliament last Friday, carries a provision that makes it mandatory for large companies to constitute audit committees. The move is designed to institutionalise a system of checks and balances that will ensure a measure of rectitude in board-level decision-making. Henceforth, companies with a paid-up equity of 50 million rupees and above will have to set up an audit committee comprising at least three directors, including whole-time directors and managing directors.
ICICI OFFLOADING SECURITISED DEBT
Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) has started offloading debentures created in place of normal loan assets in order to boost liquidity.
The Observer
AIR INDIA TRIMS LOSSES IN FIRST QUARTER

Air India cut down losses to 370 million rupees in the first quarter of the fiscal ended June 1997 as against 1.34 billion in the corresponding period in the previous year. The unaudited financial results for April-June show the airline's turnover around seven billion rupees against the targested 10 billion. The company was able to bring down its losses due to improved performace in its seat factor from 55 percent to 67 percent.
16 PORT SITES TO BE DEVELOPED BY PRIVATE SECTOR

As many as 16 ports or port sites in the country will be developed, mostly on build, operate and transfer (BOT) basis through private participation, the Union government's Directorate General of Shipping (DGS) officials said. While some of these proposals awaited the government approval, a couple of them were already being implemented.
